value.zh: 陳書卷二十一
value.en: Book of Chen, Volume 21
value.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 21

value.zh: 性耿介，絕請託，雖儲副之尊，公侯之重，溺情相及，終不為屈。
value.en: By nature he was unyielding and refused all private requests; neither the heir's rank nor the weight of dukes and marquises could make him bend.
value.literal: By nature he was unyielding and cut off all private requests; though the heir's dignity or the weight of dukes and marquises, if feeling overflowed toward him, in the end he would not bend.

value.zh: 始興王叔陵之在湘州，累諷有司，固求台鉉。
value.en: While Prince Shixing, Shuling, was in Xiangzhou, he repeatedly pressed the offices and demanded capital ministerial posts.
value.literal: When the Prince of Shixing, Shuling, was in Xiangzhou, he repeatedly hinted to the relevant offices and firmly sought capital ministerial posts.

value.zh: 奐曰：「羇章之職，本以德舉，未必皇枝。」
value.en: Huan said, "Capital memorial-review posts are raised by virtue and need not go to imperial kin."
value.literal: Huan said: "Capital memorial-review posts are by nature raised through virtue and need not be imperial kin."

value.zh: 因抗言於高宗。
value.en: He then spoke boldly to Emperor Xuan.
value.literal: He thereupon spoke boldly to Emperor Xuan.

value.zh: 高宗曰：「始興那忽望公，且朕兒為公，須在鄱陽王後。」
value.en: Emperor Xuan said, "How could Shixing suddenly want such a post? Even if my son held it, he would rank after the Prince of Poyang."
value.literal: Emperor Xuan said: "How could Shixing suddenly aspire to such a post? Besides, if my son were to hold it, he would have to come after the Prince of Poyang."

value.zh: 奐曰：「臣之所見，亦如聖旨。」
value.en: Huan said, "What I see agrees with Your Majesty's intent."
value.literal: Huan said: "What your servant sees is also as in the sacred edict."

value.zh: 後主時在東宮，欲以江總為太子詹事，令管記陸瑜言之於奐。
value.en: Houzhu was then in the eastern palace and wanted Jiang Zong as grand tutor; he had recorder Lu Yu raise it with Huan.
value.literal: Houzhu was then in the Eastern Palace and wished to make Jiang Zong Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; he had Recorder Lu Yu speak of it to Huan.

value.zh: 奐謂瑜曰：「江有潘、陸之華，而無園、綺之實，輔弼儲宮，竊有所難。」
value.en: Huan told Yu, "Jiang has Pan Yue and Lu Ji's brilliance, but not Qiuyuan and Chaofu's solid worth; as tutor to the heir I find it hard to approve."
value.literal: Huan told Yu: "Jiang has the brilliance of Pan Yue and Lu Ji, but not the solid worth of Qiuyuan and Chaofu; to assist and support the heir's palace, I privately find it difficult."

value.zh: 瑜具以白後主，後主深以為恨，乃自言於高宗。
value.en: Yu reported this fully to Houzhu, who deeply resented it and then spoke to Emperor Xuan himself.
value.literal: Yu reported it fully to Houzhu; Houzhu deeply resented it and thereupon spoke of it himself to Emperor Xuan.

value.zh: 高宗將許之，奐乃奏曰：「江總文華之人，今皇太子文華不少，豈藉於總！
value.en: Emperor Xuan was about to agree when Huan memorialized: "Jiang Zong is a literary man, but the crown prince already has brilliance enough—why need Zong?
value.literal: Emperor Xuan was about to assent; Huan then memorialized, saying: "Jiang Zong is a man of literary brilliance; the present crown prince already has no little literary brilliance—why rely on Zong!

value.zh: 如臣愚見，願選敦重之才，以居輔導。」
value.en: In my humble view, choose a man of solid weight for the tutor's post."
value.literal: In your servant's foolish view, I wish to choose a man of solid weight to occupy the post of guidance."

value.zh: 帝曰：「即如卿言，誰當居此？」
value.en: The emperor said, "If that is so, who should hold it?"
value.literal: The Emperor said: "If it is as you say, who should hold this?"

value.zh: 奐曰：「 都官尚書王廓，世有懿德，識性敦敏，可以居之。」
value.en: Huan said, "Wang Kuo, minister of justice, comes from a family of fine virtue and is solid and quick in judgment—he can hold it."
value.literal: Huan said: "Minister of Justice Wang Kuo, of a family with fine virtue through generations, knowing and by nature solid and quick, can hold it."

value.zh: 後主時亦在側，乃曰：「廓王泰之子，不可居太子詹事。」
value.en: Houzhu, who was also present, said, "Kuo is Wang Tai's son—he cannot be grand tutor."
value.literal: Houzhu was then also at the side and said: "Kuo is the son of Wang Tai—he cannot hold the post of Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince."

value.zh: 奐又奏曰：「宋朝范廚即范泰之子，亦為太子詹事，前代不疑。」
value.en: Huan memorialized again: "Under Liu Song, Fan Chu, Fan Tai's son, was grand tutor, and earlier ages raised no objection."
value.literal: Huan again memorialized, saying: "In Liu Song, Fan Chu was the son of Fan Tai and also served as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; former ages did not doubt it."

value.zh: 後主固爭之，帝卒以總為詹事，由是忤旨。
value.en: Houzhu argued stubbornly; the emperor finally made Zong grand tutor, and Huan fell foul of the throne.
value.literal: Houzhu stubbornly disputed it; the Emperor in the end made Zong Grand Tutor, and from this Huan went against the imperial intent.

value.zh: 其梗正如此。
value.en: His unyielding character was like this.
value.literal: His unyielding uprightness was like this.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 顒遣其將張方，穎遣其將陸機、牽秀、石超等來逼京師。
value.en: Zhang Fang came at the head of Prince Yong’s host, while Lu Ji, Qian Xiu, and Shi Chao advanced for Prince Ying against Luoyang.
value.literal: Yong dispatched his general Zhang Fang; Ying dispatched his generals Lu Ji, Qian Xiu, Shi Chao, and others to press the capital.

value.zh: 乙丑，帝幸十三里橋，遣將軍皇甫商距方于宜陽。
value.en: The emperor rode to the Thirteen-Li bridge and ordered Huangfu Shang to hold Zhang Fang at Yiyang on the yichou day.
value.literal: On the yichou day the emperor visited the bridge at Thirteen Li and sent General Huangfu Shang to block Zhang Fang at Yiyang.

value.zh: 己巳，帝旋軍于宣武場。
value.en: By the jisi day the imperial camp had withdrawn to the Xuanwu parade ground.
value.literal: On the jisi day the emperor wheeled the army back to the Xuanwu drill ground.

value.zh: 庚午，舍于石樓。
value.en: He spent the gengwu night at the Stone Tower.
value.literal: On the gengwu day he lodged at the Stone Tower.

value.zh: 天中裂，無雲而雷。
value.en: A fissure seemed to open in the heavens, and thunder rolled under a cloudless sky.
value.literal: The sky split midway; without clouds there was thunder.

value.zh: 冬十月壬寅，帝旋于宮。
value.en: The sovereign re-entered the palace on renyin in the tenth month.
value.literal: In winter, on the renyin day of the tenth month, the emperor returned to the palace.

value.zh: 石超焚緱氏，服御無遺。
value.en: Shi Chao put Gongshi to the torch and destroyed almost every piece of the imperial train.
value.literal: Shi Chao burned Gongshi, leaving nothing of the imperial baggage.

value.zh: 丁未，破牽秀、范陽王虓于東陽門外。
value.en: Outside the Dongyang Gate the loyalists broke Qian Xiu and Prince Xiao of Fanyang on dingwei.
value.literal: On the dingwei day Qian Xiu and Prince Xiao of Fanyang were defeated outside the Dongyang Gate.

value.zh: 戊申，破陸機于建春門，石超走，斬其大將賈崇等十六人，懸首銅駝街。
value.en: At the Jianchun Gate on wushen Lu Ji’s line collapsed, Shi Chao bolted, and sixteen of his senior commanders including Jia Chong were executed, their heads displayed along Copper Camel Street.
value.literal: On the wushen day Lu Ji was defeated at the Jianchun Gate; Shi Chao fled; sixteen of his chief generals including Jia Chong were beheaded and their heads hung along Copper Camel Street.

value.zh: 張方退屯十三里橋。
value.en: Zhang Fang pulled back to the Thirteen-Li bridge.
value.literal: Zhang Fang withdrew and encamped at the Thirteen-Li bridge.

value.zh: 傅玄
value.en: Fu Xuan
value.literal: Fu Xuan.

value.zh: 倫篡，又為右光祿、開府，加侍中。
value.en: When Lun seized the throne, Fu Zhi became right grand master of splendid horses with independent establishment and added palace attendant.
value.literal: When Lun usurped, he again was right grand master of splendid horses, established office, added palace attendant.

value.zh: 惠帝還宮，祗以經受偽職請退，不許。
value.en: After Emperor Hui returned, Fu Zhi asked to resign for having served the usurper; the court refused.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui returned to the palace, Zhi because he had received illicit office asked to retire—not permitted.

value.zh: 初，倫之篡也，孫秀與義陽王威等十餘人預撰儀式禪文。
value.en: When Lun first usurped, Sun Xiu, Prince Yiyang Sima Wei, and a dozen others had drafted the abdication liturgy and text.
value.literal: At first when Lun usurped, Sun Xiu and Prince of Yiyang, Wei, and more than a dozen others pre-drafted the ceremonies and abdication texts.

value.zh: 及倫敗，齊王冏收侍中劉逵、常侍騶捷、杜育、黃門郎陸機、右丞周導、王尊等付廷尉。
value.en: When Lun fell, Prince Qi Sima Jiong arrested Liu Dai, Zou Jie, Du Yu, Lu Ji, Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others for the commandant of justice.
value.literal: When Lun fell, the prince of Qi, Jiong, seized palace attendant Liu Dai, regular attendants Zou Jie, Du Yu, yellow gate gentleman Lu Ji, right aide Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others and handed them to the commandant of justice.

value.zh: 以禪文出中書，復議處祗罪，會赦得原。
value.en: Because the abdication edict had issued from the secretariat, some wanted Fu Zhi punished, but a general amnesty spared him.
value.literal: Because the abdication text came from the secretariat, they again debated punishing Zhi's crime, but a general amnesty arrived and he was pardoned.

value.zh: 後以禪文草本非祗所撰，於是詔復光祿大夫。
value.en: Later it was shown the draft was not his hand, and an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.
value.literal: Later because the abdication draft in manuscript was not written by Zhi, thereupon an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.

value.zh: 子宣，尚弘農公主。
value.en: His son Fu Xuan married the princess of Hongnong.
value.literal: His son Xuan married the Princess of Hongnong.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。
value.en: Storm shattered funeral umbrellas.
value.literal: When the hearse set out great wind and thunder came—canopies and coverings flew torn.

value.zh: 又為哀策曰：「皇帝臨軒，使洗馬劉務告于皇太子之殯曰：咨爾遹！
value.en: They further composed a condolence text: "The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!
value.literal: They further composed a condolence text: 'The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!

value.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。
value.en: From childhood you were outstanding, and your fine qualities flourished abundantly.
value.literal: You drew from youth heroic sap, fragrance ripe at birth.

value.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
value.en: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.
value.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.

value.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
value.en: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.
value.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.

value.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
value.en: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
value.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

value.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。
value.en: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.
value.literal: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.

value.zh: 如何凶戾潛構，禍害如茲！
value.en: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!
value.literal: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!

value.zh: 哀感和氣，痛貫四時。
value.en: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.
value.literal: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.

value.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
value.en: Alas, how grievous!
value.literal: Alas, alas the sorrow!

value.zh: 爾之降廢，實我不明。
value.en: Your degradation was truly due to my lack of discernment.
value.literal: Your degradation was truly my blindness.

value.zh: 牝亂沈烖，釁結禍成。
value.en: A woman’s disorder brought deep calamity; hostility accumulated and disaster took shape.
value.literal: Female chaos sank calamity; omens knotted into disaster.

value.zh: 爾之逝矣，誰百其形？
value.en: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?
value.literal: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?

value.zh: 昔之申生，含枉莫訟。
value.en: Long ago Shen Sheng bore false charges, with none to plead his case.
value.literal: Long ago Shen Sheng bore wrong yet could not plead.

value.zh: 今爾之負，抱冤於東。
value.en: Now you too bear unjust blame and nurse your grievance in the east.
value.literal: Now your burden of grievance hugs the eastern lands.

value.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！
value.en: Among all who understand, who would not grieve?
value.literal: Far and near anyone with insight—who fails bitter grief!

value.zh: 壺關幹主，千秋悟己。
value.en: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.
value.literal: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.

value.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。
value.en: Across different ages, the pattern is the same; past and present share one principle.
value.literal: Different age, same rule—past and present one principle.

value.zh: 皇孫啟建，隆祚爾子。
value.en: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.
value.literal: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.

value.zh: 雖悴前終，庶榮後始。
value.en: Though your own end was sorrowful, may the new beginning afterward be glorious.
value.literal: Though front end withered, rear blossom may yet flourish.

value.zh: 窀穸既營，將寧爾神。
value.en: Your burial chamber is now prepared, to bring your spirit peace.
value.literal: Burial vault now built—we pacify your spirit.

value.zh: 華髦電逝，戎車雷震。
value.en: Splendid plumes flash past like lightning; war chariots rumble like thunder.
value.literal: Flower feathers flash like lightning; war wagons thunder.

value.zh: 芒芒羽蓋，翼翼縉紳。
value.en: Feathered canopies stretch far and wide; the gentry advance in orderly ranks.
value.literal: Vast feather-canopies; crowded sash-and-hat ranks.

value.zh: 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛！
value.en: Courtiers weep together.
value.literal: Shared grief and equal pain—who lacks bitter sorrow!

value.zh: 庶光來葉，永世不泯。」
value.en: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages."
value.literal: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages.'

value.zh: 諡曰湣懷。
value.en: Canonized Crown Prince Minhuai.
value.literal: Posthumous title Minhuai was granted.

value.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。
value.en: Buried sixth month at Xianping.
value.literal: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.

value.zh: 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉。
value.en: Yan Zuan's plea built Son-Lament Terrace—Jiang Tong and Lu Ji wrote elegies.
value.literal: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.

value.zh: 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。
value.en: Three sons shared Yu's prison.
value.literal: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.

value.zh: 孫惠
value.en: Sun Hui.
value.literal: Section heading: Sun Hui.

value.zh: 孫惠，字德施，吳國富陽人，吳豫章太守賁曾孫也。
value.en: Sun Hui, whose courtesy name was Deshi, came from Fuyang in the old state of Wu and was a great-grandson of Ben, the Yuzhang grand administrator who had served Wu.
value.literal: Sun Hui, courtesy name Deshi, was a native of Fuyang in the state of Wu; he was a great-grandson of Ben, who had been Grand Administrator of Yuzhang under Wu.

value.zh: 父祖並仕吳。
value.en: Both his father and his grandfather had served the Wu regime.
value.literal: His father and grandfather both held office in Wu.

value.zh: 惠口訥，好學有才識，州辟不就，寓居蕭沛之間。
value.en: He was awkward in speech but a devoted student, with real ability and insight. Though the provincial authorities tried to appoint him, he stayed out of office and lived for a time between Xiao and Pei.
value.literal: Hui was slow of tongue, loved learning, and had talent and judgment; the province summoned him but he did not take office, and he lodged between Xiao and Pei.

value.zh: 永甯初，赴齊王冏義，討趙王倫，以功封晉興縣侯，辟大司馬戶曹掾，轉東曹屬。
value.en: When Yongning began, he joined Sima Jiong, the Prince of Qi, in the loyalist campaign against Sima Lun, the Prince of Zhao. His service earned him the county marquisate of Jinxing, a post as clerk in the minister of war's revenue office, and then a place on the eastern staff.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Yongning era, he answered Prince of Qi Jiong's call to righteous arms and campaigned against Prince of Zhao Lun; for merit he was enfeoffed marquis of Jinxing County, appointed clerk in the Revenue Bureau of the Minister of War, then transferred to a subordinate post in the eastern bureau.

value.zh: 冏驕矜僭侈，天下失望。
value.en: Jiong grew haughty and overbearing, overstepping his rank and spending on a princely scale until the empire had lost faith in him.
value.literal: Jiong was arrogant, boastful, presumptuous, and extravagant; all under Heaven were disappointed in him.

value.zh: 惠獻言於冏，諷以五難、四不可，勸令歸籓，辭甚切至。
value.en: Sun Hui laid before him a carefully framed remonstrance—the 'five difficulties' and 'four impossibilities'—urging him to withdraw to his princely domain. The tone was urgent and uncompromising.
value.literal: Hui submitted advice to Jiong, using 'five difficulties' and 'four impossibilities' as indirect admonition, urging him to return to his fief; the wording was extremely blunt and thorough.

value.zh: 冏不納。
value.en: Jiong refused to listen.
value.literal: Jiong did not accept it.

value.zh: 惠懼罪，辭疾去。
value.en: Fearing reprisals, Sun Hui pleaded illness and slipped away.
value.literal: Hui feared punishment, pleaded illness, and departed.

value.zh: 頃之，冏果敗。
value.en: Soon afterward Jiong fell, exactly as he had warned.
value.literal: Before long, Jiong indeed was defeated.

value.zh: 成都王穎薦惠為大將軍參軍、領奮威將軍、白沙督。
value.en: Sima Ying, the Prince of Chengdu, then recommended him as an adviser on the grand general's staff, with the concurrent titles of General Who Rouses Might and commander of the Baisha garrison.
value.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying recommended Hui as staff adviser to the grand general, concurrently General Who Rouses Might, and commander at Baisha.

value.zh: 是時，穎將征長沙王乂，以陸機為前鋒都督。
value.en: Ying was preparing to move against Sima Yi, the Prince of Changsha, and named Lu Ji to lead the van.
value.literal: At this time Ying was about to campaign against Prince of Changsha Yi and appointed Lu Ji as commander of the vanguard.

value.zh: 惠與機同鄉里，憂其致禍，勸機讓都督于王粹。
value.en: As a townsman of Lu Ji, Sun Hui worried the appointment would destroy him and urged him to step aside in favor of Wang Cui.
value.literal: Hui was from the same home region as Ji; fearing that Ji would bring disaster on himself, he urged Ji to yield the commander's post to Wang Cui.

value.zh: 及機兄弟被戮，惠甚傷恨之。
value.en: When Lu Ji and his brothers were put to death, Sun Hui mourned them bitterly.
value.literal: When Ji and his brothers were executed, Hui deeply grieved and resented it.

value.zh: 時惠又擅殺穎牙門將梁俊，懼罪，因改姓名以遁。
value.en: He had already killed Liang Jun, one of Ying's gate generals, without orders. Dreading the consequences, he took a new identity and went into hiding.
value.literal: At that time Hui had also on his own authority killed Liang Jun, a gate-guard general under Ying; fearing punishment, he changed his name and fled into hiding.

value.zh: 姚興
value.en: Biography of Yao Xing.
value.literal: Yao Xing.

value.en: The first installment of the account.
value.literal: (Part One)

value.zh: 興覽之大悅，謂其黃門侍郎姚文祖曰：「卿知宗敞乎？」
value.en: Yao Xing read the memorial and was greatly pleased; he asked Yao Wenzu about Zong Chang.
value.literal: Xing read it and was greatly pleased, saying to his Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Yao Wenzu: "Do you know Zong Chang?"

value.zh: 文祖曰：「與臣州裏，西方之英雋。」
value.en: He is our countryman and a western star."
value.literal: Wenzu said: "He is of my province; a splendid talent of the west."

value.zh: 興曰：「有表理王尚，文義甚佳，當王尚研思耳。」
value.en: This petition for Wang Shang is brilliant—Wang Shang must have drafted it."
value.literal: Xing said: "There is a memorial reasoning Wang Shang; the literary sense is very fine—it must be Wang Shang's polished thought."

value.zh: 文祖曰：「尚在南台，禁止不與賓客交通，敞寓於楊桓，非尚明矣。」
value.en: Yao Wenzu said, "Wang Shang is at the south terrace, forbidden to traffic with guests; Zong Chang lodges with Yang Huan—clearly Wang did not write it."
value.literal: Wenzu said: "Shang is at the south terrace, forbidden to traffic with guests; Chang lodges with Yang Huan—not Shang is clear."

value.zh: 興曰：「若爾，桓為措思乎？」
value.en: Yang Huan then?"
value.literal: Xing said: "If so, did Huan set the thought?"

value.zh: 文祖曰：「西方評敞甚重，優於楊桓。
value.en: Yao Wenzu said, "The west ranks Zong Chang very high, above Yang Huan.
value.literal: Wenzu said: "The west ranks Chang very high, above Yang Huan.

value.zh: 敞昔與呂超周旋，陛下試可問之。」
value.en: Zong Chang formerly associated with Lü Chao—Your Majesty may try asking him."
value.literal: Chang formerly circled with Lü Chao—Your Majesty may try asking him."

value.zh: 興因謂超曰：「宗敞文才何如？
value.en: He asked Lü Chao, "How is Zong Chang's literary talent?
value.literal: Xing thereupon said to Chao: "How is Zong Chang's literary talent?

value.zh: 可是誰輩？」
value.en: Who is his peer?"
value.literal: To what company does he belong?"

value.zh: 超曰：「敞在西土，時論甚美，方敞魏之陳、徐，晉之潘、陸。」
value.en: Lü Chao said, "In the western lands contemporary opinion esteems him greatly; he matches Chen Lin and Xu Gan of Wei, Pan Yue and Lu Ji of Jin."
value.literal: Chao said: "In the western lands contemporary opinion esteems him greatly; he matches Chen and Xu of Wei, Pan and Lu of Jin."

value.zh: 即以表示超曰：「涼州小地，寧有此才乎？」
value.en: He showed the memorial: could Liangzhou produce this?"
value.literal: Thereupon he showed the memorial to Chao, saying: "Can a small land like Liangzhou have such talent?"

value.zh: 超曰：「臣以敞余文比之，未足稱多。
value.en: Lü Chao said, "Compared to his other writings this does not count for much.
value.literal: Chao said: "Your subject comparing Chang's remaining writings—this does not count as much.

value.zh: 琳琅出於昆嶺，明珠生於海濱，若必以地求人，則文命大夏之棄夫，姬昌東夷之擯士。
value.en: Genius is not geography—Yu and Wen Wang came from humble ground.
value.literal: Fine jade comes from Kun range, bright pearls from the sea shore—if you must seek men by locality, then Wenming was a cast-off man of great Xia, Jichang a rejected scholar of eastern Yi.

value.zh: 但當問其文彩何如，不可以區宇格物。」
value.en: Judge the prose, not the map."
value.literal: You should only ask how the literary color is; you cannot use region to measure things."

value.zh: 興悅，赦尚之罪，以為尚書。
value.en: Yao Xing freed Wang Shang and named him director of the secretariat.
value.literal: Xing was pleased, pardoned Shang's crime, and made him Director of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 房玄齡 玄齡子遺直 遺愛 杜如晦 弟楚客 叔淹
value.en: Fang Xuanling; his sons Yizhi and Yiai; Du Ruhui, with Ruhui's younger brother Chuke and uncle Yan.
value.literal: Fang Xuanling; Xuanling's sons Yizhi and Yiai; Du Ruhui; younger brother Chuke; uncle Yan.

value.zh: 尋與中書侍郎褚遂良受詔重撰《晉書》，於是奏取太子左庶子許敬宗、中書舍人來濟、著作郎陸元仕、劉子翼、前雍州刺史令狐德棻、太子舍人李義府、薛元超、起居郎上官儀等八人，分功撰錄，以臧榮緒《晉書》爲主，參考諸家，甚爲詳洽。
value.en: Soon afterward he and Vice Director of the Secretariat Chu Suiliang were ordered to rewrite the Book of Jin. He asked that eight men share the work: Xu Jingzong, Left Mentor of the Crown Prince; Lai Ji, Drafter of the Secretariat; the editorial directors Lu Yuanshi and Liu Ziyi; Linghu Defen, former Prefect of Yongzhou; the crown prince's secretaries Li Yifu and Xue Yuanchao; and the court diarist Shangguan Yi. They took Zang Rongxu's Book of Jin as the base, compared the other traditions, and made a full and careful text.
value.literal: Soon after, together with Vice Director of the Secretariat Chu Suiliang, he received an edict to rewrite the Book of Jin; he then memorialized to take eight men—Xu Jingzong, Left Mentor of the Crown Prince; Lai Ji, Drafter of the Secretariat; Lu Yuanshi and Liu Ziyi, Editorial Directors; Linghu Defen, former Prefect of Yongzhou; Li Yifu and Xue Yuanchao, Secretaries of the Crown Prince; and Shangguan Yi, Court Diarist—to divide the work of compiling the record, taking Zang Rongxu's Book of Jin as the principal text and consulting the various other families, and it was very detailed and complete.

value.zh: 然史官多是文詠之士，好採詭謬碎事，以廣異聞；
value.en: But most of the historians were men of verse, fond of gathering strange, dubious scraps to swell the store of oddities;
value.literal: Yet the historians were mostly men of literary verse, fond of gathering strange, false, and trivial matters in order to broaden curious hearsay;

value.zh: 又所評論，競爲綺豔，不求篤實，由是頗爲學者所譏。
value.en: and their judgments vied in ornate color rather than solid truth, so scholars rather mocked the work.
value.literal: and the comments they made competed in ornate beauty and did not seek solid substance; for this they were rather ridiculed by scholars.

value.zh: 唯李淳風深明星曆，善於著述，所修《天文》、《律曆》、《五行》三志，最可觀採。
value.en: Only Li Chunfeng knew the stars and the calendar thoroughly and wrote well. His three treatises—Heavenly Patterns, Pitch-pipes and the Calendar, and the Five Phases—are the parts most worth reading.
value.literal: Only Li Chunfeng was deeply versed in the stars and the calendar and skilled at writing; the three treatises he compiled—Heavenly Patterns, Pitch-pipes and the Calendar, and the Five Phases—are the most worth viewing and adopting.

value.zh: 太宗自著宣、武二帝及陸機、王羲之四論，於是總題云「御撰」。
value.en: Taizong himself wrote the four discourses on Emperors Xuan and Wu and on Lu Ji and Wang Xizhi, and the whole work was then titled 'Imperially Compiled.'
value.literal: Taizong himself wrote the four discourses on Emperors Xuan and Wu and on Lu Ji and Wang Xizhi, and thereupon the work was titled as a whole 'Imperially Compiled.'

value.zh: 至二十年，書成，凡一百三十捲，詔藏於秘府，頒賜加級各有差。
value.en: In the twentieth year the book was finished, one hundred thirty juan in all. An edict stored it in the imperial library, and gifts and promotions were given in differing degrees.
value.literal: By the twentieth year the book was completed, in all one hundred thirty scrolls; an edict stored it in the secret archives, and grants and advancements of rank were each according to difference.

value.zh: 馬懷素，潤州丹徒人也。
value.en: Ma Huai Su was a native of Dantu in Run Prefecture.
value.literal: Ma HuaiSu—Ma HuaiSu was a native of Dantu in Run Prefecture.

value.zh: 寓居江都，少師事李善。
value.en: He lived in Jiangdu and in his youth studied under Li Shan.
value.literal: He resided in Jiangdu and in his youth took Li Shan as his teacher.

value.zh: 家貧無燈燭，晝采薪蘇，夜燃讀書，遂博覽經史，善屬文。
value.en: His family was too poor to afford lamps or candles; by day he gathered firewood and brush, and by night he burned them to read by their light. In this way he came to be widely versed in the classics and histories and skilled at writing.
value.literal: His family was poor and had no lamps or candles; by day he gathered firewood and kindling, by night he burned them to read, and thus came to read broadly in the classics and histories and was skilled at literary composition.

value.zh: 舉進士，又應制舉，登文學優贍科，拜郿尉，四遷左臺監察御史。
value.en: He passed the jinshi examination and also took the special imperial literary examination, placing in the Literary Excellence and Abundant Talent category. He was appointed magistrate of Mei district and was promoted four times to investigating censor of the Left Censorate.
value.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, also responded to the imperial examination, attained the Literary Excellence and Abundant Talent category, was appointed Mei district magistrate, and was transferred four times to Left Censorate investigating censor.

value.zh: 初，無量與馬懷素俱為侍讀，顧待甚厚；
value.en: Earlier, when Wuliang and Ma Huai Su had both served as imperial readers, they had been favored and treated with great generosity;
value.literal: Earlier, when Wuliang and Ma HuaiSu had both served as imperial readers, they were favored and treated very generously;

value.zh: 及無量等卒後，秘書少監康子原、國子博士侯行果等又入侍講，雖屢加賞賜，而禮遇不逮褚焉。
value.en: after Wuliang and the others died, Secretariat vice director Kang Ziyuan, National University erudite Hou Xingguo, and others again served as lecturers. Although they were repeatedly rewarded, the courtesy shown them did not equal what had been accorded Chu.
value.literal: after Wuliang and the others died, Secretariat vice director Kang Ziyuan, National University erudite Hou Xingguo, and others again entered to lecture, and although rewards were repeatedly increased, the courtesy shown did not reach that given to Chu.

value.zh: 劉子玄，本名知幾，楚州刺史胤之族孫也。
value.en: Liu Zixuan, whose original name was Zhiji, was a clansman of Chu Prefecture governor Liu Yinzhi.
value.literal: Liu Zixuan—Liu Zixuan, original name Zhiji, was a clansman of Chu Prefecture governor Yinzhi.

value.zh: 少與兄知柔俱以詞學知名，弱冠舉進士，授獲嘉主簿。
value.en: In his youth he and his elder brother Zhirou were both famed for literary learning. At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Huojia.
value.literal: In youth he and his elder brother Zhirou were both famed for literary learning; at the capping age he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Huojia chief clerk.

value.zh: 證聖年，有制文武九品已上各言時政得失，知幾上表陳四事，詞甚切直。
value.en: In the Zhengsheng year an edict required civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above to comment on current policy. Zhiji submitted a memorial on four matters in very blunt and direct language.
value.literal: In the Zhengsheng year an edict ordered civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above each to speak on the gains and losses of current policy; Zhiji submitted a memorial setting forth four matters, his wording very blunt and direct.

value.zh: 是時官爵僭濫而法網嚴密，士類競為趨進而多陷刑戮，知幾乃著《思慎賦》以刺時，且以見意。
value.en: At that time offices and titles were lavished without restraint while the law was harsh; scholars scrambled for advancement and many fell victim to punishment. Zhiji therefore wrote Reflections on Caution to satirize the age and make his views known.
value.literal: At that time offices and titles were excessively bestowed while the legal net was strict; gentlemen strove to advance and many fell into punishment and execution. Zhiji therefore composed Reflections on Caution to satirize the age and also to express his intent.

value.zh: 鳳閣侍郎蘇味道、李嶠見而嘆曰：「陸機《豪士》所不及也。」
value.en: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Ministers Su Weidao and Li Jiao, on reading it, exclaimed, "Even Lu Ji's Bold Heroes does not equal this."
value.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Su Weidao and Li Jiao, on reading it, sighed and said: "Even Lu Ji's Bold Heroes does not reach this."

value.zh: 梁書卷第四十 列傳第三十四
value.en: Book of Liang, Volume 40, Biography 34
value.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 40, Biography 34

value.zh: 顯幼而聰敏，當世號曰神童。
value.en: Xian was bright from childhood; men of his day called him a prodigy.
value.literal: Xian was clever from childhood; his contemporaries called him a divine child.

value.zh: 天監初，舉秀才，解褐中軍臨川王行參軍，俄署法曹。
value.en: When Tianjian opened he was presented as a cultivated talent, entered service as staff officer to the Prince of Linchuan in the Central Army, and soon headed the law bureau.
value.literal: At the opening of Tianjian he was recommended as a cultivated talent, relieved his clerk’s collar as Administrative Officer on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan in the Central Army, and soon served as Chief of the Law Bureau.

value.zh: 顯好學，博涉多參通，任昉嘗得一篇缺簡書，文字零落，歷示諸人，莫能識者，顯云是《古文尚書》所刪逸篇，昉檢《周書》，果如其說，昉因大相賞異。
value.en: Xian loved study and ranged across many disciplines; once Ren Fang had a bamboo slip with characters broken and faded, showed it around, and no one could read it—Xian said it was a lost passage cut from the Old Text Documents; Fang checked the Documents of Zhou and found it exact, and from then held him in wonder.
value.literal: Xian loved learning and ranged widely in many fields; once Ren Fang obtained a fragmentary bamboo text with characters scattered and eroded, showed it to everyone, and none could read it—Xian said it was a lost passage deleted from the Old Text Documents, and when Fang checked the Documents of Zhou it matched exactly; Fang was thereafter greatly struck by him.

value.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，尚書令沈約命駕造焉，於坐策顯經史十事，顯對其九。
value.en: After his mother’s mourning, the Director of the Department of State Affairs Shen Yue came by carriage to call on him and, seated, examined him on ten points of canon and history—Xian answered nine.
value.literal: When his mother’s mourning ended, the Director of the Department of State Affairs Shen Yue came in his carriage to visit, and at the seat tested Xian on ten matters from the classics and histories—Xian answered nine.

value.zh: 約曰：「老夫昏忘，不可受策；
value.en: Yue said, “This old man is dim and forgetful; I cannot sit for your test—
value.literal: Yue said: “This old man is muddled and forgetful; I cannot submit to examination—

value.zh: 雖然，聊試數事，不可至十也。」
value.en: Still, try me on a few—you must not make it ten.”
value.literal: Even so, let me try a few things—you must not reach ten.”

value.zh: 顯問其五，約對其二。
value.en: Xian put five questions to him; Yue answered two.
value.literal: Xian questioned him on five; Yue answered two.

value.zh: 陸倕聞之歎曰：「劉郎可謂差人，雖吾家平原詣張壯武，王粲謁伯喈，必無此對。」
value.en: Lu Chui heard and sighed, “Master Liu is a man apart—even when our Lu Ji sought out Zhang Hua, or Wang Can called on Cai Yong, there was never such an exchange.”
value.literal: Lu Chui heard of it and sighed: “One may say Master Liu is a man apart—even when our house’s Lu Ji called on Zhang Hua, or when Wang Can visited Cai Yong, there could not have been such parry and riposte.”

value.zh: 其爲名流推賞如此。
value.en: So the leading men of the age honored him.
value.literal: Such was the esteem in which leading minds held him.

value.zh: 及約爲太子少傅，乃引爲五官掾，俄兼廷尉正。
value.en: When Yue became mentor to the heir apparent, he drew Xian in as aide in the Five Offices; soon Xian also served as director under the Court of Judicial Review.
value.literal: When Yue became Mentor to the Heir Apparent, he brought Xian in as Aide in the Five Offices, and soon he also served as Director under the Court of Judicial Review.

value.zh: 五兵尚書傅昭掌著作，撰國史，引顯爲佐。
value.en: Fu Zhao, Minister of the Five Armies and overseer of historiography, was compiling the national history and took Xian as his assistant.
value.literal: Fu Zhao, Minister of the Five Armies and in charge of historiography, was compiling the national history and brought Xian in as assistant.

value.zh: 九年，始革尚書五都選，顯以本官兼吏部郎，又除司空臨川王外兵參軍，遷尚書儀曹郎。
value.en: In year nine the five selection directorates were first reformed; Xian kept his post while also serving as director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made external military officer to the Minister of Works, the Prince of Linchuan, and then Gentleman of the Ceremonial Bureau.
value.literal: In year nine the Ministry system was first reformed for the five directorates of selection; Xian in his existing post also served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, was further appointed External Military Officer to the Minister of Works, the Prince of Linchuan, and was transferred to Gentleman of the Ceremonial Bureau.

value.zh: 嘗爲《上朝詩》，沈約見而美之，時約郊居宅新成，因命工書人題之於壁。
value.en: He once wrote a poem on the morning audience; Shen Yue admired it, and when Yue’s suburban house was newly finished he had a scribe brush it on the wall.
value.literal: Once he composed a poem on morning audience; Shen Yue read it with admiration, and at the time Yue’s suburban residence was newly built—he had a scribe paint it on the wall.

value.zh: 出爲臨川王記室參軍。
value.en: He left the capital as recorder to the Prince of Linchuan.
value.literal: He went out as Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan.

value.zh: 建康平，復入爲尚書儀曹侍郎，兼中書通事舍人。
value.en: After Jiankang was pacified he returned as vice director of ceremonial affairs and again Master of Documents for Palace Affairs.
value.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he returned as Vice Director of Ceremonial Affairs in the Ministry of Rites and concurrently Master of Documents for Palace Affairs.

value.zh: 出爲秣陵令，又除驃騎鄱陽王記室，兼中書舍人，累遷步兵校尉、中書侍郎，舍人如故。
value.en: He served as magistrate of Moling, then recorder to the Prince of Poyang, Cavalry General, again Master of Documents, and rose to Commandant of Footsoldiers and Secretariat gentleman, keeping the palace post throughout.
value.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Moling, was again made Recorder to the Prince of Poyang, Cavalry General, with concurrent service as Master of Documents, and was promoted in succession to Commandant of Footsoldiers and Gentleman of the Secretariat, still Master of Documents.

value.zh: 到沆 丘遲 劉苞 袁峻 庾於陵 弟肩吾 劉昭 何遜 鍾嶸 周興嗣 吳均
value.en: Dao Hang · Qiu Chi · Liu Bao · Yuan Jun · Yu Yuling · Jianwu (brother) · Liu Zhao · He Xun · Zhong Rong · Zhou Xingsi · Wu Jun
value.literal: Dao Hang, Qiu Chi, Liu Bao, Yuan Jun, Yu Yuling, younger brother Jianwu, Liu Zhao, He Xun, Zhong Rong, Zhou Xingsi, Wu Jun

value.zh: 氣之動物，物之感人，故搖盪性情，形諸舞詠。
value.en: Qi moves things; things move people—so feeling stirs and finds form in dance and song.
value.literal: When qi stirs things, things move people; thus feelings sway and take shape in dance and song.

value.zh: 欲以照燭三才，輝麗萬有，靈祇待之以致饗，幽微藉之以昭告。
value.en: It lights the three powers and adorns the myriad; spirits wait on it for sacrifice, the hidden use it to declare.
value.literal: It means to illuminate the three realms and shed glory on the myriad beings; spirits await it for offerings, and the hidden and subtle rely on it for proclamation.

value.zh: 動天地，感鬼神，莫近於詩。
value.en: To move Heaven and Earth and touch gods and ghosts, nothing nears poetry.
value.literal: Moving Heaven and Earth, touching spirits and ghosts—nothing comes nearer than poetry.

value.zh: 昔《南風》之辭，《卿雲》之頌，厥義夐矣。
value.en: Of old Southern Winds and Cloud-Coach—their meaning was already vast.
value.literal: Of old the words of the *Southern Winds* and the hymn *Cloud-Coach*—their meaning was already far-reaching.

value.zh: 《夏歌》曰「郁陶乎予心」，楚謠云「名余曰正則」，雖詩體未全，然略是五言之濫觴也。
value.en: Xia Songs have "deeply troubled in heart"; Chu songs name "Zhengze"—verse form was incomplete, yet these were the springs of five-character poetry.
value.literal: The *Xia Songs* say "I am deeply troubled in heart"; a Chu song says "They named me Zhengze"—though the poetic form was not yet complete, they were roughly the source of five-character verse.

value.zh: 逮漢李陵，始著五言之目。
value.en: By Han, Li Ling first established five-character verse as a category.
value.literal: Down to Han's Li Ling, the category of five-character verse was first set forth.

value.zh: 古詩眇邈，人代難詳，推其文體，固是炎漢之制，非衰周之倡也。
value.en: Ancient poems are distant and ages obscure; by form they belong to Han, not late Zhou.
value.literal: Ancient poems are remote and ages hard to trace; judging their form, they are truly products of blazing Han, not songs of declining Zhou.

value.zh: 自王、揚、枚、馬之徒，辭賦競爽，而吟詠靡聞。
value.en: From Wang Bao, Yang Xiong, Mei Cheng, and Sima Xiangru on, fu competed in brilliance while lyric verse was rarely heard.
value.literal: From Wang, Yang, Mei, and Ma onward, rhapsodies vied in brilliance, yet lyric singing was scarcely heard.

value.zh: 從李都尉訖班婕妤，將百年間，有婦人焉，一人而已。
value.en: From Li Ling to Lady Ban, nearly a century held one woman poet—and only one.
value.literal: From Commandant Li to Lady Ban, in nearly a hundred years there was a woman—and only one.

value.zh: 詩人之風，頓已缺喪。
value.en: The poets' wind had suddenly died away.
value.literal: The poets' tradition had suddenly perished.

value.zh: 東京二百載中，唯有班固《詠史》，質木無文致。
value.en: Eastern Han's two centuries held only Ban Gu's Ode on History—plain and without literary grace.
value.literal: In the two hundred years of Eastern Han there was only Ban Gu's *Ode on History*—plain wood without literary grace.

value.zh: 降及建安，曹公父子，篤好斯文；
value.en: By Jian'an, the Cao lord and his sons deeply loved letters;
value.literal: Down to the Jian'an period, Lord Cao and his sons deeply loved this craft;

value.zh: 平原兄弟，鬱爲文棟；
value.en: the Pingyuan brothers rose as literary pillars;
value.literal: the brothers of Pingyuan flourished as literary pillars;

value.zh: 劉楨、王粲，爲其羽冀。
value.en: Liu Zhen and Wang Can were their wings.
value.literal: Liu Zhen and Wang Can were their wings.

value.zh: 次有攀龍託鳳，自致於屬車者，蓋將百計。
value.en: Next came nearly a hundred who clung to dragons and phoenixes and joined the train.
value.literal: Next came those who, clinging to dragons and nesting phoenixes, attached themselves to the rear train—nearly a hundred in number.

value.zh: 彬彬之盛，大備於時矣！
value.en: Such abundant flowering was complete in that age!
value.literal: Such abundant flourishing was fully prepared in that age!

value.zh: 爾後陵遲衰微，訖於有晉。
value.en: Afterward it declined to Jin.
value.literal: Afterward it declined and weakened, down to Jin.

value.zh: 太康中，三張二陸，兩潘一左，勃爾復興，踵武前王，風流未沫，亦文章之中興也。
value.en: Taikang saw the three Zhangs, two Lus, two Pans, and Zuo Zuo revive the art—wind not yet spent, a literary revival.
value.literal: In the Taikang era the three Zhangs, two Lus, two Pans, and one Zuo suddenly flourished again, following the martial ways of former kings; the breeze had not yet dried—this too was a literary revival.

value.zh: 永嘉時，貴黃、老，尚虛談，于時篇什，理過其辭，淡乎寡味。
value.en: Yongjia honored Huang-Lao and pure talk; verse reasoned past its words—thin and flavorless.
value.literal: In the Yongjia era Yellow Lao and empty talk were honored; poems of the time reasoned beyond their words and were thin and tasteless.

value.zh: 爰及江表，微波尚傳，孫綽、許詢、桓、庾諸公，皆平典似《道德論》，建安之風盡矣。
value.en: South of the river slight ripples remained; Sun Chuo, Xu Xun, Huan, and Yu wrote level pieces like the Dao De Lun—Jian'an's wind was gone.
value.literal: Reaching the lands south of the Yangtze, slight ripples still passed on; Sun Chuo, Xu Xun, Huan, Yu, and the gentlemen were all level and canonical like the *Dao De Lun*—Jian'an's wind was wholly gone.

value.zh: 先是郭景純用俊上之才，創變其體；
value.en: Earlier Guo Jingchun, with lofty talent, changed the form;
value.literal: Earlier Guo Pu, with lofty talent, innovated and changed the form;

value.zh: 劉越石仗清剛之氣，贊成厥美。
value.en: Liu Yueshi, with pure firm spirit, helped perfect that beauty.
value.literal: Liu Kun, relying on pure firmness, helped perfect that beauty.

value.zh: 然彼衆我寡，未能動俗。
value.en: Yet the many outweighed the few and could not shift custom.
value.literal: Yet they were many against few and could not move custom.

value.zh: 逮義熙中，謝益壽斐然繼作；
value.en: By Yixi Xie Lingyun flourished and continued writing;
value.literal: By the Yixi era Xie Lingyun flourished and continued the work;

value.zh: 元嘉初，有謝靈運，才高辭盛，富豔難蹤，固已含跨劉、郭，陵轢潘、左。
value.en: Early Yuanjia brought Xie Lingyun—great talent, rich diction, splendor hard to follow; he spanned Liu and Guo and towered over Pan and Zuo.
value.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia there was Xie Lingyun—talent high, diction rich, splendor hard to track; he already spanned Liu and Guo and towered over Pan and Zuo.

value.zh: 故知陳思爲建安之傑，公幹、仲宣爲輔；
value.en: Thus Prince Si was Jian'an's crown, Gonggan and Zhongxuan his aides;
value.literal: Thus we know Prince Si was Jian'an's paragon, with Gonggan and Zhongxuan as aides;

value.zh: 陸機爲太康之英，安仁、景陽爲輔；
value.en: Lu Ji was Taikang's hero, Anren and Jingyang his aides;
value.literal: Lu Ji was Taikang's hero, with Anren and Jingyang as aides;

value.zh: 謝客爲元嘉之雄，顏延年爲輔：此皆五言之冠冕，文辭之命世。
value.en: Guest Xie was Yuanjia's champion, Yan Yannian his aide—these crown five-character verse and master an age of letters.
value.literal: Guest Xie was Yuanjia's champion, with Yan Yannian as aide: these are the crowns of five-character verse, fated masters of letters.

value.zh: 高帝十九男：昭皇后生武帝、豫章文獻王嶷；
value.en: Emperor Gao had nineteen sons: Empress Zhao bore Emperor Wu and Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang, Ni;
value.literal: Emperor Gao had nineteen sons: Empress Zhao bore Emperor Wu and Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang Ni;

value.zh: 謝貴嬪生臨川獻王映、長沙威王晃；
value.en: Noble Consort Xie bore Prince Xian of Linchuan, Ying, and Prince Wei of Changsha, Huang;
value.literal: Noble Consort Xie bore Prince Xian of Linchuan Ying and Prince Wei of Changsha Huang;

value.zh: 羅太妃生武陵昭王曄；
value.en: Consort Dowager Luo bore Prince Zhao of Wuling, Ye;
value.literal: Consort Dowager Luo bore Prince Zhao of Wuling Ye;

value.zh: 任太妃生安成恭王暠；
value.en: Consort Dowager Ren bore Prince Gong of Ancheng, Gao;
value.literal: Consort Dowager Ren bore Prince Gong of Ancheng Gao;

value.zh: 陸修儀生鄱陽王鏘、晉熙王 銶；
value.en: Lady of Cultivated Rites Lu bore the Prince of Poyang, Qiang, and the Prince of Jinxi, Qiu;
value.literal: Lady of Cultivated Rites Lu bore Prince of Poyang Qiang and Prince of Jinxi Qiu;

value.zh: 袁修容生桂陽王鑠；
value.en: Lady of Cultivated Appearance Yuan bore the Prince of Guiyang, Shuo;
value.literal: Lady of Cultivated Appearance Yuan bore Prince of Guiyang Shuo;

value.zh: 何太妃生始興簡王鑒、宜都王鏗；
value.en: Consort Dowager He bore Prince Jian of Shixing, Jian, and the Prince of Yidu, Keng;
value.literal: Consort Dowager He bore Prince Jian of Shixing Jian and Prince of Yidu Keng;

value.zh: 區貴人生衡陽王鈞；
value.en: Honorable Lady Qu bore the Prince of Hengyang, Jun;
value.literal: Lady of the District Qu bore Prince of Hengyang Jun;

value.zh: 張淑妃生江夏王鋒、河東王鉉；
value.en: Imperial Beauty Zhang bore the Prince of Jiangxia, Feng, and the Prince of Hedong, Xuan;
value.literal: Imperial Beauty Zhang bore Prince of Jiangxia Feng and Prince of Hedong Xuan;

value.zh: 李美人生南平王銳；
value.en: Lady of Beauty Li bore the Prince of Nanping, Rui;
value.literal: Lady of Beauty Li bore Prince of Nanping Rui;

value.zh: 第九、第十三、第十四、第 十七皇子早亡。
value.en: The ninth, thirteenth, fourteenth, and seventeenth princes died in childhood.
value.literal: The ninth, thirteenth, fourteenth, and seventeenth princes died young.

value.zh: 衡陽王鈞出繼元王后。
value.en: The Prince of Hengyang, Jun, was given in adoption to succeed the Prince of Yuan.
value.literal: Prince of Hengyang Jun was adopted out to succeed the Prince of Yuan.

value.zh: 武陵昭王曄，字宣照，太祖第五子也。
value.en: Prince Zhao of Wuling, Ye, styled Xuanzhao, was the founding emperor's fifth son.
value.literal: Prince Zhao of Wuling Ye, styled Xuanzhao, was the founding emperor's fifth son.

value.zh: 母羅氏，從太祖在淮陰，以罪誅，曄年四歲，思慕不異成人，故每見愛。
value.en: His mother was Lady Luo; she had followed the founding emperor at Huaiyin and was executed; at four Ye grieved like a grown man — and was always cherished for it.
value.literal: His mother was the Luo clan; she followed the founding emperor at Huaiyin and was executed for a crime; Ye at four years mourned with longing no different from an adult — therefore he was always loved.

value.zh: 初除冠軍將軍，轉征虜將軍。
value.en: He was first champion general, then General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
value.literal: He was first made champion general, then transferred General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

value.zh: 曄剛穎俊出， 工弈棋，與諸王共作短句，詩學謝靈運體，以呈上，報曰：「見汝二十字，諸兒作中最為優者。
value.en: Ye was sharp and outstanding, skilled at chess; with his brothers he wrote short verses in Xie Lingyun's style and presented them; the emperor replied: "In your twenty characters this is the best of the boys' work.
value.literal: Ye was forceful and outstanding, skilled at chess; with the other princes he composed short verses in Xie Lingyun's manner and presented them; the reply said: "Seeing your twenty characters — among the boys' work this is finest.

value.zh: 但康樂放蕩，作體不辨有首尾，安仁、士衡深可宗尚，顏延之抑 其次也。」
value.en: Yet Lingyun is unrestrained — his pieces lack clear beginning and end; Pan Yue and Lu Ji are truly worth emulating; Yan Yanzhi ranks beneath them."
value.literal: Yet Lingyun is unrestrained — his pieces have no clear head or tail; Anren and Shiheng are truly to be honored; Yan Yanzhi ranks below them."

value.zh: 建元三年，出為持節、都督會稽東陽新安永嘉臨海五郡軍事、會稽太守，將軍如故。
value.en: In Jianyuan year three he went out bearer of credentials, commander of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai, and governor of Kuaiji, rank unchanged.
value.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan he went out bearer of credentials, commander of military affairs in five commanderies — Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai — and governor of Kuaiji, general as before.

value.zh: 上遣儒士劉瓛往郡，為曄講《五經》。
value.en: The emperor sent the scholar Liu Huan to lecture Ye on the Five Classics in his commandery.
value.literal: The emperor sent the scholar Liu Huan to the commandery to lecture Ye on the Five Classics.

value.zh: 南齊書卷四十二‧列傳第二十三
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 42, Biographies 23
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 42, Biographies 23

value.zh: 史臣曰：士死知己，蓋有生所共情，雖愚智之品有二，而逢迎之運唯一。
value.en: The Historian says: For a gentleman to die for one who knows him is a feeling common to all who live; though wit and folly divide men into two kinds, the fortune of winning favor is singular.
value.literal: The Historian says: For a gentleman to die for one who knows him is an emotion shared by all who live; though in wit and folly there are two grades, the fortune of winning favor is one alone.

value.zh: 夫懷可知之才，受知人之眄，無慚外物，此固天理，其猶藏在中心，銜恩念報。
value.en: When one possesses talent that can be recognized and receives the favor of one who knows men, unashamed before the world—this is the way of heaven itself, as though grace were stored in the heart and repayment always in mind.
value.literal: When one harbors talent that can be known and receives the glance of one who knows men, without shame before outward things—this is indeed the way of heaven; it is as though stored within the heart, cherishing grace and thinking of repayment.

value.zh: 況乎義早蕃僚，道同遇合，踰越勝己，顧邁先流，弃子如遺，曾微舊德，使狗之喻，人致前譏，慚包疚心，我無其事。
value.en: How much more when men were joined early as feudal staff, united in purpose through mutual encounter, surpassing those above them and looking back beyond those who came before, casting off their sons as though they were nothing and scarcely remembering old kindness—the simile of the dog invites reproach from others; ashamed and guilty in heart, I for my part have no such deed.
value.literal: How much the more when they were bound early as feudal staff, united in the Way through mutual encounter, surpassing those better than themselves, looking back and exceeding those who came before, casting off sons as though forgotten, scarcely heeding old grace—the simile of the dog makes others bring forward reproof; burdened with shame and guilt in heart, I for my part have no such deed.

value.zh: 嗚呼！
value.en: Alas!
value.literal: Alas!

value.zh: 陸機所以賦豪士也。
value.en: This is why Lu Ji wrote his rhapsody on the proud knight.
value.literal: This is why Lu Ji composed his rhapsody on the proud knight.

value.zh: 列傳第十七
value.en: the seventeenth year of Biographies
value.literal: Biographies 17

value.zh: 性耿介，絕諸請托，雖儲副之尊，公侯之重，溺情相及，終不為屈。
value.en: Stubbornly upright, he refused every pull of patronage—even when crown princes or great lords pleaded on private grounds, he would not bend.
value.literal: By nature he was upright and severed all requests for favor; though the heir's dignity or the weight of dukes and marquises pressed him with personal feeling, he never yielded.

value.zh: 始興王叔陵之在湘州，累諷有司，固求台鉉。
value.en: Prince Shixing's son Shuling, while governing Xiang Province, repeatedly leaned on officials to demand a capital appointment.
value.literal: When Prince Shixing's Shuling was in Xiang Province he repeatedly hinted to the relevant offices and stubbornly sought a post at the capital.

value.zh: 奐曰：「袞章本以德重，未必皇枝。」
value.en: Huan replied, "Grand seals belong to men of moral weight, not automatically to princes of the blood."
value.literal: Huan said, "The imperial regalia of office rests on weight of virtue—not necessarily on imperial descent."

value.zh: 因抗言于宣帝。
value.en: He spoke bluntly against the demand before Emperor Xuan.
value.literal: He therefore spoke boldly against this to Emperor Xuan.

value.zh: 帝曰：「始興那忽望公，且朕兒為公，須在鄱陽王后。」
value.en: The emperor said, "Shixing should not dream so high—and as my son he stands below the Queen of Poyang in precedence."
value.literal: The emperor said, "How could Shixing harbor such hopes? And as my son he ranks after the Queen of Poyang."

value.zh: 奐曰：「臣之所見，亦如聖旨。」
value.en: Huan answered, "My view matches Your Majesty's own."
value.literal: Huan said, "What I see accords with Your Majesty's intent."

value.zh: 後主時在東宮，欲以江總為太子詹事，令管記陸瑜言之奐。
value.en: The future Later Lord, then crown prince, wanted Jiang Zong as Grand Tutor and sent his recorder Lu Yu to sound Huan out.
value.literal: At the time the Later Lord was in the Eastern Palace and wished to make Jiang Zong Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent; he had his recorder Lu Yu speak to Huan about it.

value.zh: 奐曰：「江有潘、陸之華，而無園、綺之實，輔弼儲貳，竊謂非材。」
value.en: Huan said, "Jiang has Pan Yue's polish and Lu Ji's glitter, not Yuan Ji's depth or Qi Wuhui's substance—he is no fit tutor for an heir."
value.literal: Huan said, "Jiang has the brilliance of Pan and Lu but not the substance of Yuan and Qi; to assist the heir I privately deem him unfit."

value.zh: 後主深以為恨，乃自言于宣帝。
value.en: The crown prince nursed a deep grudge and complained directly to Emperor Xuan.
value.literal: The Later Lord deeply resented this and spoke of it himself to Emperor Xuan.

value.zh: 宣帝將許之，奐乃奏曰：「江總文華之人，今皇太子文華不少，無藉於總。
value.en: Emperor Xuan nearly agreed until Huan memorialized: "Jiang Zong is ornamental prose—the crown prince already has ornament enough without him.
value.literal: Emperor Xuan was about to consent; Huan then memorialized: "Jiang Zong is a man of literary brilliance; the Crown Prince already has brilliance enough and has no need of Zong.

value.zh: 如臣愚見，願選敦重之才，以居輔導。」
value.en: I urge appointing a man of sober weight to guide the heir."
value.literal: In my humble view, I wish to select a man of solid weight to occupy the guiding post."

value.zh: 帝曰：「誰可？」
value.en: The emperor asked, "Whom do you propose?"
value.literal: The emperor said, "Who would do?"

value.zh: 奐曰：「都官尚書王廓，代有懿德，識性敦敏，可以居之。」
value.en: Huan named Wang Kuo of the Palace Bureau—'a line of proven virtue, sharp and steady—he can hold the post."
value.literal: Huan said, "Wang Kuo, Minister of the Palace Bureau, comes from generations of fine virtue and is discerning and earnest—he can hold the post."

value.zh: 後主時亦在側，乃曰：「廓王泰之子，不可居太子詹事。」
value.en: The crown prince, present at the audience, objected: "Wang Kuo is Wang Tai's son—unsuitable for Grand Tutor."
value.literal: The Later Lord was also at the side and said, "Kuo is Wang Tai's son—he cannot hold the Grand Tutorship to the Heir Apparent."

value.zh: 奐又曰：「宋朝范曄即範泰之子，亦為太子詹事。」
value.en: Huan countered, "Under Song, Fan Ye—Fan Tai's own son—served as Grand Tutor."
value.literal: Huan again said, "In the Song dynasty Fan Ye, who was Fan Tai's son, also served as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent."

value.zh: 後主固爭之，帝以總為詹事，由是忤旨。
value.en: The prince pressed his case; the emperor named Jiang Zong Grand Tutor anyway, and Huan fell from favor.
value.literal: The Later Lord stubbornly contested; the emperor made Zong Grand Tutor, and Huan thereby offended the imperial intent.

value.zh: 列傳第三十三齊高帝諸子下
value.en: Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Southern Qi, Part Two
value.literal: Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Qi, Part Two

value.zh: 性剛穎俊出，與諸王共作短句詩，學謝靈運體，以呈高帝。
value.en: His temperament was bold, sharp, and outstanding; with the other princes he wrote short poems in the manner of Xie Lingyun and presented them to Emperor Gao.
value.literal: His nature was firm, sharp, and outstanding; with the other princes he composed short-verse poems in Xie Lingyun's style and presented them to Emperor Gao.

value.zh: 帝報曰：「見汝二十字，諸兒作中，最為優者。
value.en: The emperor replied: "I have seen your twenty lines—among all my sons' compositions, yours is the finest.
value.literal: The emperor replied: "Seeing your twenty characters—among all the boys' compositions yours is the finest.

value.zh: 但康樂放蕩，作體不辨有首尾，安仁、士衡深可宗尚，顏延之抑其次也。」
value.en: But Kangyue is unrestrained—his compositions lack clear structure from beginning to end. Anren and Shiheng are truly worthy of emulation; Yanzhi ranks below them."
value.literal: But Xie Kangyue is unrestrained; his compositional form does not distinguish beginning from end. Pan Anren and Lu Shiheng are deeply worthy of reverence; Yan Yanzhi ranks below them."

value.zh: 及延興元年，明帝誅高、武、文惠諸子，鏗聞之，馮左右從容雅步，詠陸機吊魏武云：「昔以四海為己任，死則以愛子托人。」
value.en: In the first year of Yanxing, when Emperor Ming killed the sons of Gao, Wu, and Wenhu, Qiang heard of it and, supported by his attendants, walked with easy, graceful steps, reciting Lu Ji's elegy for Cao Cao: "Once he took the four seas as his charge; in death he entrusted his beloved son to another."
value.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, when Emperor Ming killed the sons of Gao, Wu, and Wenhu, Qiang heard of it and, leaning on his attendants, walked with easy, graceful steps, reciting Lu Ji's elegy for Emperor Wu of Wei: "Once he took the four seas as his charge; in death he entrusted his beloved son to another."

value.zh: 如此者三，左右皆泣。
value.en: He did this three times; all around him wept.
value.literal: He did this three times; those around all wept.

value.zh: 後果遣呂文顯賚藥往，夜進聽事，正逢八關齋。
value.en: Later Lü Wenxian was sent with poisoned medicine; at night he entered the audience hall, just as the Eightfold Fast was being observed.
value.literal: Later Lü Wenxian was indeed sent with poisoned medicine; at night he entered the audience hall, just as the Eightfold Fast was being observed.

value.zh: 鏗上高坐，謂文顯曰：「高皇昔寵任君，何事乃有今日之行？」
value.en: Qiang sat on a high seat and said to Wenxian, "Emperor Gao once favored and trusted you—why this action today?"
value.literal: Qiang sat on a high seat and said to Wenxian, "Emperor Gao once favored and trusted you—why today's action?"

value.zh: 答云：「出不獲已。」
value.en: He answered, "I had no choice."
value.literal: He answered, "I could not do otherwise."

value.zh: 於是仰藥。
value.en: He therefore swallowed the medicine.
value.literal: He therefore swallowed the medicine.

value.zh: 時年十八。
value.en: He was eighteen years old.
value.literal: He was then eighteen years old.

value.zh: 身長七尺，鏗狀似兄嶷，咸以國器許之。
value.en: He stood seven chi tall; Qiang resembled his elder brother Ying in appearance, and all regarded him as fit for the highest office.
value.literal: He stood seven chi in height; Qiang's appearance resembled his elder brother Ying, and all regarded him as material for the state.

value.zh: 及死，有識者莫不痛惜。
value.en: At his death all who knew him grieved.
value.literal: At his death all who knew him grieved.

value.zh: 文皇帝諱丕，字子桓，武帝太子也。
value.en: Emperor Wen—whose personal name was Pi and courtesy name Zihuan—was the heir apparent of Emperor Wu (Cao Cao).
value.literal: Emperor Wen, taboo name Pi, courtesy name Zihuan, was the heir son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 中平四年冬，生于譙。
value.en: He was born at Qiao in the winter of the fourth year of the Zhongping era (187 CE).
value.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Zhongping, he was born in Qiao.

value.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：帝生時，有雲氣青色而圜如車盖當其上，終日，望氣者以爲至貴之證，非人臣之氣。
value.en: 〈The Wei Book records that at his birth a greenish aura hung above him in a disk like a carriage canopy for the whole day; diviners of qi pronounced it the sign of supreme eminence—not the kind of portent that attends an ordinary minister.
value.literal: 〈The Wei Book says: When the Emperor was born, there was green cloud vapor, round like a carriage canopy, suspended above him all day; those who read auspicious vapors took it as proof of the utmost nobility, not the aura of a mere subject.

value.zh: 年八歲，能屬文。
value.en: At eight he could already write polished compositions.
value.literal: At age eight, he could compose connected literary pieces.

value.zh: 有逸才，遂博貫古今經傳諸子百家之書。
value.en: Gifted with extraordinary ability, he went on to command the classics and their commentaries and the writings of the hundred schools past and present.
value.literal: He had outstanding talent, and thereupon broadly mastered the classics and commentaries and the writings of the hundred schools from ancient to modern times.

value.zh: 善騎射，好擊劔。
value.en: He excelled at horsemanship and archery and delighted in swordplay.
value.literal: He was skilled at riding and archery, and fond of fencing.

value.zh: 舉茂才，不行。
value.en: Nominated as a "flourishing talent," he declined to serve.
value.literal: He was recommended as a maocai (flourishing talent), but did not take office.

value.zh: 《獻帝起居注》曰：建安十五年，爲司徒趙溫所辟。
value.en: According to the Daily Records of Emperor Xian, in Jian'an 15 (210 CE) he was recruited by Minister of Education Zhao Wen.
value.literal: The Daily Records of Emperor Xian says: In the fifteenth year of Jian'an, he was summoned by Minister of Education Zhao Wen.

value.zh: 太祖表「溫辟臣子弟，選舉故不以實」。
value.en: The Grand Progenitor memorialized: "Zhao Wen has summoned my sons and younger relatives; therefore the selection is not according to reality."
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor memorialized: "Zhao Wen has summoned my sons and younger relatives; therefore the selection is not according to reality."

value.zh: 使侍中守光祿勳郗慮持節奉策免溫官。〉
value.en: He had Palace Attendant and acting Supervisor of the Household Xi Lu carry the credential and deliver the edict stripping Zhao Wen of his post.〉
value.literal: He ordered Palace Attendant acting Supervisor of the Household Xi Lu, bearing the insignia, to present the edict and dismiss Zhao Wen from office.〉

value.zh: 建安十六年，爲五官中郎將、副丞相。
value.en: In Jian'an 16 (211 CE) he was appointed General of the Household for All Purposes and deputy to the Chancellor.
value.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an, he became General of the Household for All Purposes and deputy to the Chancellor.

value.zh: 二十二年，立爲魏太子。
value.en: In the twenty-second year of Jian'an (217 CE) he was named heir apparent of Wei.
value.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was established as heir apparent of Wei.

value.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：太祖不時立太子，太子自疑。
value.en: 〈The Wei Summary notes that Cao Cao had long delayed naming an heir, and the crown prince began to doubt his position.
value.literal: 〈The Wei Summary says: The Grand Progenitor did not promptly establish an heir apparent; the heir apparent himself grew doubtful.

value.zh: 是時有高元呂者，善相人，乃呼問之，對曰：「其貴乃不可言。」
value.en: There was a physiognomist named Gao Yuanlü whom Pi summoned and questioned; Gao answered, "The degree of eminence is beyond words."
value.literal: At this time there was a man named Gao Yuanlü who was skilled at physiognomy; he was summoned and asked, and replied: "His nobility cannot be described in words."

value.zh: 問：「壽幾何？」
value.en: Pi asked, "How long will he live?"
value.literal: He was asked: "How long will his lifespan be?"

value.zh: 元呂曰：「其壽，至四十當有小苦，過是無憂也。」
value.en: Gao Yuanlü replied, "He will meet a brief ordeal at forty; after that, nothing to fear."
value.literal: Yuanlü said: "As for his lifespan, when he reaches forty there will be a small hardship; beyond that there will be no worries."

value.zh: 後無幾而立爲王太子，至年四十而薨。〉
value.en: Soon afterward Pi was installed as heir apparent of the King of Wei; he died in his fortieth year.
value.literal: Not long afterward he was established as heir apparent of the king; he reached age forty and died.

value.zh: 太祖崩，嗣位爲丞相、魏王。
value.en: When Cao Cao died, Pi succeeded him as Chancellor and King of Wei.
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor died; he succeeded to the posts of Chancellor and King of Wei.

value.zh: 〈袁宏《漢紀》載漢帝詔曰：「魏太子丕：昔皇天授乃顯考以翼我皇家，遂攘除羣凶，拓定九州，弘功茂績，光于宇宙，朕用垂拱負扆二十有餘載。
value.en: 〈Yuan Hong's Han Annals preserves an imperial edict: "Heir apparent Pi of Wei: High Heaven once entrusted your late father to uphold Our house; he crushed the rebels, pacified the Nine Regions, and left achievements that fill heaven and earth—while I, leaning on the cushions at court, reigned at ease for more than twenty years.
value.literal: 〈Yuan Hong's Han Annals carries an edict of the Han Emperor: "Wei heir apparent Pi: Formerly August Heaven entrusted your illustrious father to aid Our royal house; thereupon he swept away the multitude of villains and expanded and settled the Nine Provinces; his grand merit and abundant deeds shine through the universe; I therefore leaned on the rail with folded arms for more than twenty years.

value.zh: 天不憖遺一老，永保余一人，早世潛神，哀悼傷切。
value.en: Heaven would not spare one wise elder to shelter Me alone; he left the world too soon, and My sorrow cuts deep.
value.literal: Heaven is not willing to leave Us one elder to forever protect Us alone; he departed the world early and concealed his spirit; Our grief and mourning are cutting.

value.zh: 丕奕世宣明，宜秉文武，紹熙前緒。
value.en: Pi carries forward a luminous succession; he should wield both civil and military authority and carry on the work begun before him.
value.literal: Pi in successive generations shines brightly; he should grasp civil and military affairs and continue and brighten the former threads.

value.zh: 今使使持節御史大夫華歆奉策詔授丕丞相印綬、魏王璽紱，領冀州牧。
value.en: I therefore dispatch Bearer of the Imperial Insignia and Imperial Counselor Hua Xin to deliver the edict investing Pi with the Chancellor's seal and ribbon, the regalia of the King of Wei, and the governorship of Ji Province.
value.literal: Now sending Bearer of the Imperial Insignia Imperial Counselor Hua Xin to present by edict and confer on Pi the Chancellor's seal-cord, the King of Wei's seal and ribbon, and headship as Governor of Ji Province.

value.zh: 方今外有遺虜，遐夷未賔，旗鼓猶在邊境，干戈不得韜刃，斯乃播揚洪烈，立功垂名之秋也。
value.en: Barbarians still linger beyond the frontiers, distant peoples have not yet come to court, signal drums stand posted along the borders, and arms cannot yet be laid aside—this is the very hour to broadcast great deeds and win lasting fame.
value.literal: At present beyond Us there remain remnant barbarians; distant tribes have not yet submitted; banners and drums are still at the borders; weapons cannot sheath their blades—this is indeed the autumn season for spreading abroad mighty deeds and establishing merit to leave a name.

value.zh: 豈得脩諒闇之禮，究曾、閔之志哉？
value.en: How could you confine yourself to solitary mourning like a common heir or imitate only the filial retreats of Zengzi and Min Ziqian?
value.literal: How can one observe the rites of silent mourning in the dark chamber and exhaust the intentions of Zeng and Min?

value.zh: 其敬服朕命，抑弭憂懷，旁祗厥緒，時亮庶功，以稱朕意。
value.en: Therefore obey this charge with reverence: set anxiety aside, uphold the legacy on every side, and in due course bring every task to fruition, that My wishes may be fulfilled.
value.literal: Respectfully obey Our command; suppress and extinguish anxious thoughts; broadly reverence its continuation; seasonally brighten the various achievements, thereby matching Our intention.

value.zh: 於戲，可不勉與！」〉
value.en: Ah—how could you do otherwise than strive with all your might!"〉"
value.literal: Alas, can you not exert yourself!"〉"

value.zh: 尊王后曰王太后。
value.en: The queen consort was elevated to Queen Dowager of Wei.
value.literal: The queen consort was honored as Queen Dowager of the King.

value.zh: 改建安二十五年爲延康元年。
value.en: The twenty-fifth year of Jian'an was redesignated the first year of the Yan Kang era (220 CE).
value.literal: He changed the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an to be the first year of Yan Kang.

value.zh: 冬十一月癸卯，令曰：「諸將征伐，士卒死亡者或未收斂，吾甚哀之；
value.en: On the guimao day in the eleventh month of winter he issued an edict: "When armies march, fallen soldiers are sometimes left unburied—I mourn them bitterly;
value.literal: Winter, eleventh month, on Guimao, an edict said: "When the various generals campaign and soldiers die, sometimes they are not gathered for burial—I deeply grieve for them;

value.zh: 其告郡國給槥
value.en: instruct every commandery and principality to issue coffins
value.literal: let it be announced to the commanderies and kingdoms to supply hui (coffins)

value.zh: 〈槥音衞〉
value.en: 〈Pronunciation gloss: the character (hui) is read the same as the common word wei, "defend."〉
value.literal: 〈 hui is pronounced wei 〉

value.zh: 櫝殯斂，送致其家，官爲設祭。」
value.en: For encoffining and laying out the remains, ship each body home, and let the officials sponsor the sacrificial offerings."
value.literal: enclosed burial receptacles for laying out and dressing the dead, convey them to their homes, and let officials perform sacrifices for them."

value.zh: 〈《漢書》高祖八月令曰：「士卒從軍死，爲槥。」
value.en: 〈The Han shu quotes Emperor Gaozu's eighth-month decree: "Men who die on campaign shall receive a burial coffin (hui)."
value.literal: 〈The Han Book August edict of Emperor Gaozu said: "Soldiers who die following the army—supply hui."

value.zh: 應劭曰：「槥，小棺也，今謂之櫝。」
value.en: Ying Shao glosses: "Hui is a small coffin—today we call it a case (du)."
value.literal: Ying Shao said: "Hui is a small coffin; nowadays it is called du (case)."

value.zh: 應璩百一詩曰：「槥車在道路，征夫不得休。」
value.en: Ying Qu's "Hundred and One" poems say: "Coffin wagons line the roads while conscripts never rest."
value.literal: Ying Qu's Hundred and One Poem says: "The hui cart is on the road; the campaigner cannot rest."

value.zh: 陸機大墓賦曰：「觀細木而悶遲，覩洪櫝而念槥。」〉
value.en: Lu Ji's Rhapsody on a Princely Tomb says: "The sight of plain boards brought gloom; the great outer coffin recalled the simple hui."〉
value.literal: Lu Ji's Rhapsody on the Great Tomb says: "Gazing on fine wood I am depressed and slow; beholding a great case I think of hui."〉

value.zh: 丙午，行至曲蠡。
value.en: On the bingwu day he marched as far as Quli.
value.literal: On Bingwu, traveling reached Quli.

value.zh: 孫靜字幼臺，堅季弟也。
value.en: Sun Jing, styled Youtai, was the youngest of Sun Jian’s brothers.
value.literal: Sun Jing, courtesy name Youtai, was the youngest younger brother of Sun Jian.

value.zh: 堅始舉事，靜糾合鄉曲及宗室五六百人以為保障，眾咸附焉。
value.en: When Sun Jian first rose in arms, Sun Jing rallied some five or six hundred local men and kinsmen as a protective force, and people flocked to him.
value.literal: When Sun Jian first raised troops, Jing gathered five or six hundred men from the villages and the clan to serve as a safeguard, and the masses all attached themselves to him.

value.zh: 策破劉繇，定諸縣。
value.en: Sun Ce defeated Liu Yao and brought the counties under control.
value.literal: Ce defeated Liu Yao and pacified the various counties.

value.zh: 進攻會稽，遣人請靜，靜將家屬與策會於錢唐。
value.en: He pressed the attack on Kuaiji, sent for Sun Jing, and Sun Jing brought his household to join Sun Ce at Qiantang.
value.literal: Advancing to attack Kuaiji, he sent someone to summon Jing; Jing led his family members and met Ce at Qiantang.

value.zh: 是時太守王朗拒策於固陵，策數渡水戰，不能克。
value.en: The prefect Wang Lang held Sun Ce off at Guling; Sun Ce tried more than once to force a crossing and fight on the other bank but could not break through.
value.literal: At that time the Administrator Wang Lang resisted Ce at Guling; Ce several times crossed the water to give battle but could not overcome him.

value.zh: 靜說策曰："朗負阻城守，難可卒拔。
value.en: Sun Jing urged Sun Ce: Wang Lang is dug in behind natural barriers; you cannot expect to storm him overnight.
value.literal: Jing urged Ce, saying, Lang relies on natural obstacles and defends the city; he is hard to take in a hurry.

value.zh: 查瀆南去此數十里，
value.en: Zha Creek lies a few dozen li to the south,
value.literal: Zha Creek is several tens of li south of here,

value.zh: 〈查音祖加反。〉
value.en: 〈The marginal gloss indicates that Zha takes its initial from zu and its rime from jia.〉
value.literal: 〈Note on pronunciation: the character for Zha is read zu-jia [fanqie].〉

value.zh: 而道之要徑也，宜從彼據其內，所謂攻其無備、出其不意者也。
value.en: That route is the vital approach; thrust inland along it and strike where they do not expect you.
value.literal: and it is a crucial path; you ought to advance by that route and seize what lies within—what is called striking where they are unprepared and catching them unawares.

value.zh: 吾當自帥眾為軍前隊，破之必矣。
value.en: I will lead the main body myself as the first wave—we will crack them for certain.
value.literal: I shall personally lead the host as the vanguard of the army; we will surely break them.

value.zh: "策曰："善。
value.en: Sun Ce replied, Good.
value.literal: Ce said, Good.

value.zh: "乃詐令軍中曰："頃連雨水濁，兵飲之多腹痛，令促具罌缶數百口澄水。
value.en: Then he put out a false order: The river has been silty from all this rain; men who drink it are doubled up with cramps—have them ready hundreds of jars at once to draw off clear water.
value.literal: Then he falsely announced to the army: The rains have lately turned the water muddy; the soldiers drinking it have mostly gotten stomachaches—order them quickly to prepare several hundred jars and pots to settle the water.

value.zh: "至昏暮，羅以然火誑朗，便分軍夜投查瀆道，襲高遷屯。
value.en: At nightfall he lit decoy fires to fool Wang Lang, split his force, and marched up the Zha Creek track after dark to strike the camp at Gaoxian.
value.literal: At dusk he spread fires to deceive Lang, then divided the army and by night sent them along the Zha Creek road to raid the Gaoxian camp.

value.zh: 〈臣松之案：今永兴县有高迁桥。〉
value.en: 〈Pei Songzhi notes that Gaoxian Bridge still stands in present-day Yongxing County.〉
value.literal: 〈Pei Songzhi’s investigation: today in Yongxing County there is a Gaoxian Bridge.〉

value.zh: 朗大驚。
value.en: Wang Lang was thrown into panic.
value.literal: Lang was greatly alarmed.

value.zh: 遣故丹楊太守周昕等帥兵前戰。
value.en: He dispatched the former Danyang prefect Zhou Xin and others to take the lead with their men.
value.literal: He sent the former Danyang Administrator Zhou Xin and others to lead troops forward into battle.

value.zh: 策破昕等，斬之，遂定會稽。
value.en: Sun Ce routed them, killed Zhou Xin, and settled Kuaiji.
value.literal: Ce defeated Xin and the others, beheaded them, and thereupon pacified Kuaiji.

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：昕字大明。
value.en: 〈According to the Kuaiji dianlu, Zhou Xin’s courtesy name was Daming.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji Canon Record states: Xin’s courtesy name was Daming.

value.zh: 少游京师，师事太傅陈蕃，博览群书，明於风角，善推灾异。
value.en: He had studied in the capital under Grand Tutor Chen Fan, read widely, and was adept at astrological signs and reading portents.
value.literal: In his youth he traveled to the capital and studied under Grand Tutor Chen Fan; he read widely and was skilled in “wind-angle” divination and interpreting anomalies.

value.zh: 辟太尉府，举高第，稍迁丹杨太守。
value.en: He entered the Grand Commandant’s service, graduated with highest honors, and rose step by step to prefect of Danyang.
value.literal: He was summoned to the Grand Commandant’s office, ranked at the top of his cohort, and was gradually promoted to Danyang Administrator.

value.zh: 曹公起义兵，昕前后遣兵万餘人助公征伐。
value.en: When Cao Cao raised his coalition army, Zhou Xin repeatedly sent him upward of ten thousand men for the campaigns.
value.literal: When Duke Cao raised the righteous army, Xin in succession sent more than ten thousand troops to assist the duke in his expeditions.

value.zh: 袁术之在淮南也，昕恶其淫虐，绝不与通。
value.en: While Yuan Shu occupied Huainan, Zhou Xin abhorred his cruelty and dissipation and would have nothing to do with him.
value.literal: When Yuan Shu was in Huainan, Xin detested his debauchery and cruelty and utterly refused dealings with him.

value.zh: 献帝春秋曰：袁术遣吴景攻昕，未拔，景乃募百姓敢从周昕者死不赦。
value.en: The Xiandi Chunqiu records that Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing against Zhou Xin without reducing him; Wu Jing then threatened the populace that anyone who sided with Zhou Xin would die without mercy.
value.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian states: Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing to attack Xin but did not capture him; Jing then promised the common people that whoever dared follow Zhou Xin would be put to death without pardon.

value.zh: 昕曰：“我则不德，百姓何罪？”
value.en: Zhou Xin said, If I am the one at fault, what have the people done wrong?
value.literal: Xin said, If I lack virtue, what crime have the common people committed?

value.zh: 遂散兵，还本郡。〉
value.en: So he sent his soldiers home and withdrew to his own commandery.
value.literal: Thereupon he dispersed his troops and returned to his native commandery.

value.zh: 表拜靜為奮武校尉，欲授之重任，靜戀墳墓宗族，不樂出仕，求留鎮守。
value.en: Sun Ce recommended him as Colonel Who Inspires Martial Might and meant to give him a major post, but Sun Jing was unwilling to leave his family graves and kin and asked instead to stay and hold the territory.
value.literal: [Sun Ce] memorialized and appointed Jing Colonel Who Inspires Martial Might, wishing to give him heavy responsibility; Jing was attached to his ancestral graves and clan and did not relish leaving office, and asked to remain to guard and hold the region.

value.zh: 策從之。
value.en: Sun Ce agreed.
value.literal: Ce granted his request.

value.zh: 權統事，就遷昭義中郎將，終於家。
value.en: When Sun Quan took charge, Sun Jing was promoted in place to General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Righteousness and ended his days at home.
value.literal: When Quan assumed direction of affairs, [Jing] was promoted on the spot to General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Righteousness and died at home.

value.zh: 有五子，皓、瑜、皎、奐、謙。
value.en: He had five sons—Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.
value.literal: He had five sons: Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.

value.zh: 皓三子：綽、超、恭。
value.en: Sun Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.
value.literal: Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.

value.zh: 超為偏將軍。
value.en: Sun Chao rose to General of the Left.
value.literal: Chao served as General of the Left.

value.zh: 恭生峻。
value.en: Sun Gong was the father of Sun Jun.
value.literal: Gong fathered Jun.

value.zh: 綽生綝。
value.en: Sun Chuo was the father of Sun Lin.
value.literal: Chuo fathered Lin.

value.zh: 鄰年九歲，代領豫章，近封都鄉侯。
value.en: Sun Lin took Yuzhang at nine and soon received the marquisate of Dou township.
value.literal: At age nine Lin replaced him as leader of Yuzhang and was shortly enfeoffed Marquis of Dou Township.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：邻字公达，雅性精敏，幼有令誉。〉
value.en: 〈The Wu shu: Sun Lin, styled Gongda, was acute and polished and famed even as a boy.〉
value.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: Lin’s courtesy name was Gongda; by nature he was refined, keen, and from youth had a fine reputation.〉
